questions.question: An urn contains 10 black and 5 white balls. Two balls are drawn from the urn one after the other without replacement. What is the probability that both drawn balls are black?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total black balls = 10

Total white balls = 5

Total balls = 15

**Formula Used:**

Probability of drawing two black balls without replacement = (Probability of drawing the first black ball) × (Probability of drawing the second black ball after the first one is drawn)

**Calculation:**

Probability of drawing the first black ball = 10/15

Probability of drawing the second black ball after the first one is drawn = 9/14

⇒ Probability of drawing two black balls = (10/15) × (9/14)

⇒ Probability of drawing two black balls = (10 × 9) / (15 × 14)

⇒ Probability of drawing two black balls = 90 / 210

⇒ Probability of drawing two black balls = 3/7

**The probability that both drawn balls are black is 3/7.**

questions.question: In which of the following decades was India's population growth recorded as a negative growth rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "__1911 - 1921__". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the most recent census, India's population has grown, yet between 1911 and 1921, it actually decreased.
 
• Before 1921, both male and female children had poor life expectancy rates at birth.
 
• Famines and epidemics were the leading causes of population reduction.
 
• Famine, pestilence, and influenza deaths slowed the country's population growth.
 
• There was an *increase in population* from 1901 to 1911.
 
• Due to the absence of famines and epidemics during this time, resulting in a significant* drop* in the country's death rate, the population expanded by roughly 158 lakh.
 
• However, between *1911 and 1921*, the nation's growth rate slowed.
 
• The 1918 influenza outbreak contributed to a rise in mortality and the death of *140 lakh people* nationwide.
 
• *Famine*, the *plague*, and *malaria* were further factors in the population reduction.
 
• The year 1951 is frequently referred to as the year of the population explosion since there was a significant* increase in population *after 1951.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Growth of Population 

​Phase I 

 
• The period from 1901-1921 is referred to as a period of the stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India’s population, since in this period growth rate was very low, even recording a negative growth rate during 1911-1921.
 
• Both the birth rate and death rate were high keeping the rate of increase low.
 
• Poor health and medical services, illiteracy of people at large, and inefficient distribution system of food and other basic necessities were largely responsible for high birth and death rates in this period.

Phase II 

 
• The decades 1921-1951 are referred to as the period of steady population growth.
 
• An overall improvement in health and sanitation throughout the country brought down the mortality rate.
 
• At the same time, better transport and communication systems improved distribution systems.
 
• The crude birth rate remained high in this period leading to a higher growth rate than the previous phase.
 
• This is impressive in the backdrop of the Great Economic Depression, the 1920s, and World War II.

Phase III 

 
• The decades 1951-1981 are referred to as the period of population explosion in India, which was caused by a rapid fall in the mortality rate but a high fertility rate of population in the country.
 
• The average annual growth rate was as high as 2.2 percent.
 
• It is in this period, after the Independence, that developmental activity was introduced through a centralized planning process and the economy started showing up ensuring the improvement of the living conditions of people at large.
 
• Consequently, there was a high natural increase and a higher growth rate.
 
• Besides, increased international migration bringing in Tibetans, Bangladeshis, Nepalese and even people from Pakistan contributed to the high growth rate.

Phase IV 

 
• In the post-1981 till present, the growth rate of country’s population though remained high, has started slowing down gradually.
 
• A downward trend of crude birth rate is held responsible for such population growth.
 
• This was, in turn, affected by an increase in the mean age at marriage, improved quality of life particularly education of females in the country.
 
• The growth rate of population is, however, still high in the country, and it has been projected by World Development Report that the population of India will touch 1,350 million by 2025.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 37 and their LCM is 740. If one of the numbers is 148, then the other is:

⇒ 27380 = 148 × x

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head to aid and advice the president, who shall exercise his/her functions in accordance to the advice?

__
 
• **Article 74(1)** of the Constitution of India deals with the formation and role of the Council of Ministers in the Indian government.
 
• The Article mandates the formation of a Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, to **assist the President**.
 
• The advice given by the Council of Ministers is binding on the President after the** 42nd Amendment to the Constitution in 1976.**
 
• The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers effectively **hold executive power,** while the President's role is largely ceremonial in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In cases where the punishment or sentence is for an offence against any law related to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends.
 
• In cases of punishment by a court-martial.
 
• In cases where the sentence is a death sentence.
 
 
 
• **Article 73(1)** defines the extent of the executive power of the Union (Central Government)
 
 
• The executive power of the Union extends to matters on which Parliament has the power to legislate, i.e., matters in the Union List and Concurrent List (with conditions).
 
• The executive power of the Union also extends to giving directions to states where necessary for ensuring compliance with laws made by Parliament.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio of 6 : 5. If the perimeter of the field is 110 m, then what will be the breadth (in m)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of length to breadth of the rectangular field = 6 : 5

Perimeter of the field = 110 m

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

**Calculation:**

Let the length be 6x and the breadth be 5x.

Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

⇒ 110 = 2 × (6x + 5x)

⇒ 110 = 2 × 11x

⇒ 110 = 22x

⇒ x = 110 / 22

⇒ x = 5

Breadth = 5x = 5 × 5 = 25 m

**The breadth of the rectangular field is 25 m.**

questions.question: Which of the following are the fastest seismic waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• P-waves travel the fastest through the Earth's interior, with speeds ranging from** 5 to 8 km/s **in the Earth's crust and even faster in the mantle and core.
 
• P-waves are compressional waves or longitudinal waves, meaning they move through the Earth by compressing and expanding the material in the direction the wave is traveling.
 
• P-waves can** travel through solids, liquids, and gases**, which allows them to be the first waves detected by seismographs during an earthquake.
 
• Due to their high speed, P-waves are the **first seismic waves** to be recorded at any seismic station after an earthquake, hence the name primary waves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secondary Waves (S-Waves) are **Slower than P-waves (approximately 60% the speed of P-waves), traveling around 3-4 km/s in the Earth's crust.
 
• S-waves can only travel through solids (they **cannot travel through liquids or gases**, which is why they do not propagate through Earth's outer core).
 
• Oceanic waves caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on Earth’s oceans are called **Tidal waves**.
 
• Tidal waves are not related to seismic activity or earthquakes. Instead, they are caused by the **cyclic rising and falling of sea levels due to the gravitational forces exerted by the moon and the sun.**
 
• **Seismic waves** travel along the surface of the Earth, rather than through the interior.
 
• Surface waves are slower than both** P-waves and S-waves, **but they tend to be the most destructive.

questions.question: A cistern 8 m long and 4 m wide contains water up to a depth of 1 m 22 cm. Then the total area of the wet surface is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the cistern = 8 m

Width of the cistern = 4 m

Depth of the water = 1 m 22 cm = 1.22 m

**Formula Used:**

Total area of the wet surface = Area of the base + Area of the four walls

**Calculation:**

Area of the base = Length × Width

⇒ Area of the base = 8 × 4 = 32 m²

Area of the two longer walls = 2 × (Length × Depth)

⇒ Area of the two longer walls = 2 × (8 × 1.22)

⇒ Area of the two longer walls = 2 × 9.76 = 19.52 m²

Area of the two shorter walls = 2 × (Width × Depth)

⇒ Area of the two shorter walls = 2 × (4 × 1.22)

⇒ Area of the two shorter walls = 2 × 4.88 = 9.76 m²

Total area of the wet surface = Area of the base + Area of the two longer walls + Area of the two shorter walls

⇒ Total area of the wet surface = 32 + 19.52 + 9.76 = 61.28 m²

**The total area of the wet surface is 61.28 m².**
